editorialSections.title: Ask a generic AI the one question that matters. Watch it fail.

blocks.text: Large language models fail most confidently exactly where a drug program's stakes are highest: pathway and exclusivity facts. Same question, two answers. The fluent-but-wrong generic reply, and the primary-source-grounded one. The distance between them is what a wrong assumption costs your runway.
✕ Generic LLM · unsourced
"My small-molecule NCE gets orphan designation — how many years of market protection is that, and does designation itself block generics?"
"Orphan designation gives you 7 years of exclusivity that starts the day FDA designates the drug, and it blocks all generics for the whole condition — so you're protected from filing onward."
Confident. Fluent. Wrong on three counts — and wrong in the exact way that mis-sequences a launch, a raise, or a partnering term sheet.
✓ Aloha AI · primary-source grounded 21 CFR · FDCA
Same question, answered from the record:

Designation is not exclusivity. Orphan-drug exclusivity is 7 years but runs from the date of marketing approval, not from designation (21 CFR §316.31). It protects only the approved indication or use — not the whole rare disease — and can be broken if the holder can't assure supply.

Separately, a small-molecule new active moiety may earn 5-year NCE data exclusivity under Hatch-Waxman (a generic may file a Paragraph IV ANDA at year 4). Orphan and NCE exclusivity are distinct clocks that can overlap. Plan to both.
Confidence: High Why you can rely on it: it maps to 21 CFR Part 316, the FDCA exclusivity provisions, and FDA guidance, cited below with retrieval dates.
OEG — the Operator Execution Gap — is the distance between what AI says and what a regulated sponsor can act on. Closing it is the entire job.

editorialSections.title: Ask a generic AI whether your data is safe. Watch it reassure you into a breach.

blocks.text: Large language models fail most confidently exactly where a compliance officer's stakes are highest. Same question, two answers: the fluent-but-wrong reassurance, and the framework-grounded one. The distance between them is what a wrong assumption costs when it lands on privileged or PHI-bearing data.
✕ Generic LLM · unsourced
"Can we put PHI and privileged case files into ChatGPT — enterprise plans don't train on our data, right?"
"Yes — on an enterprise or business plan, OpenAI doesn't train on your data, so it's fine to use it on confidential and regulated material."
Confident. Fluent. Dangerously incomplete — it collapses four different questions (training, retention, sub-processors, human review, BAA coverage) into one, and answers only the easy one.
✓ Aloha AI · framework grounded HIPAA · Priv. · GDPR
Same question, answered from the frameworks:

"Doesn't train on you" is true but not the whole risk. By default, enterprise API inputs/outputs are still retained for a limited abuse-monitoring window (commonly up to ~30 days) unless zero-data-retention (ZDR) is separately approved for eligible endpoints. ZDR does not cover the consumer web app your staff may actually be using.

For PHI, no training claim substitutes for a signed BAA. Without one the vendor is an unauthorized third party and the transmission itself can be the disclosure (45 CFR §164.504(e)). For privileged material, routing client confidences through a tool whose terms permit disclosure can undercut confidentiality; use walled/enterprise channels, not public tools.
Confidence: High Why you can rely on it: it maps to the operative HIPAA BAA rule, published vendor retention terms, and GDPR Art. 28 sub-processor duties, cited below, with retrieval dates.
OEG (the Operator Execution Gap) is the distance between what AI says and what a regulated organization can act on. Closing it is the entire job.

editorialSections.title: Ask a generic AI why your reach dropped. Watch it guess.

blocks.text: Ask the tools most creators reach for and you get engagement folklore: post consistently, use trending audio, add hashtags. None of it names the policy mechanism that actually suppressed the post. Same question, two answers. The distance between them is why the "fix" never works.
✕ Generic AI · engagement folklore
"My evidence-based supplement post got no reach. Why, and how do I fix it?"
"The algorithm probably deprioritized it for low engagement. Post more consistently, use 20–30 trending hashtags, hook viewers in the first 3 seconds, and repost at peak times. Reach will recover."
Confident. Generic. Wrong about the cause — so every "fix" treats a policy problem as a scheduling problem, and the throttle stays exactly where it was.
✓ Aloha AI · platform-policy grounded Policy category
Same post, diagnosed against the actual policy surface:

The suppression is a claims problem, not a schedule problem. Phrases that imply a direct physiological effect, such as "boosts metabolism," "balances hormones," or "detoxifies," fall under platforms' health-and-wellness / unproven-claims category, which restricts distribution and ad eligibility regardless of how many studies you attach.

The EDSA fix: keep the Evidence, reframe the claim as discussion rather than promise, respect the reader's self-determination ("here's what the research explores" not "this will fix you"), and give a compliant action. Same rigor, inside the policy line.

Confidence: High Why you can rely on it: it maps to published platform health-and-wellness policy categories and the LegitScript ad-eligibility gate, described in the method ledger below, with review dates.
OEG (the Operator Execution Gap) is the distance between what AI says caused a problem and what actually did. Naming the real mechanism is the entire job.

editorialSections.title: A repeatable audit method, not a one-off reach hack

blocks.text: Every Aloha AI audit runs the same three-stage pipeline, so the diagnosis holds up against the next policy update, not just the current feed.
Regulatory Intelligence Layer (RIL)

Read the actual policy surfaces: published platform content and ad standards, health-and-wellness categories, and certification requirements, captured with source and review date. No engagement folklore.
Resolve to an Operator Layer (ROL) via EDSA

Raw policy becomes a content decision you can act on: which claim to reframe, which link to move, what to certify. Structured as Evidence · Discussion · Self-determination · Action, it closes the Operator Execution Gap.
Auto-refresh & alert

Platform policies change often. The audit re-checks its policy sources on a schedule (Upstash · Vercel · Exa) and can ping you when a standard shifts, so your content system doesn't drift back into suppression.
